The Social Stock Exchange (SSE) is an up-and-coming initiative of the Central Government, and is regulated by SEBI. The SSE is meant to help non-profit organisations raise funding as well as enable funders to support initiatives in a regulated environment.

Hemant Gupta heads the SSE at the Bombay Stock Exchange. In July, we invited him to speak with our team, partners and members of the larger social ecosystem to understand how the SSE can play a role for the development sector and bring up questions that can help improve it. In this clip, he demystifies how the different instruments under SSE function. Full video is now up on the Rainmatter Foundation YouTube channel.

Akshayakalpa is a farmer-entrepreneurship initiative and India’s first certified organic milk brand. They work with farmers to set up and manage small dairy farms along with providing them training, equipment, and technical support. Akshayakalpa's farms are designed to be sustainable and environmentally friendly, and they use a closed-loop system to manage waste as well. By efficiently utilising tech in agriculture and developing a sustainable model for agriculture, Akshayakalpa is paving way for the idea that small farmer-led collectives have immense potential and can ensure a better future for the planet and people.

Here, Shashi Kumar, one of Akshayakalpa’s Founders and its CEO dives deep into the story, vision and importance of initiatives like Akshayakalpa in an easy-going conversation with Hansi Mehrotra.
